name: Maria von Burgund
kurzbeschreibung:
**

Discover the Legacy of Maria von Burgund in Innsbruck

** In the heart of the **Alpenland Tirol**, the historic city of **Innsbruck** invites you to step back in time and explore the fascinating story of **Maria von Burgund**, one of Europe’s most influential medieval rulers. **

A Royal Connection to the Golden Age

** As the daughter of Emperor **Karl der Kühne** (Charles the Bold) and heiress to the powerful **Burgundian Netherlands**, **Maria von Burgund** played a pivotal role in shaping the political landscape of the 15th century. Though her reign was short-lived, her marriage to **Maximilian I**, the future Holy Roman Emperor, forged a bond that would unite the Habsburgs with Burgundy—and ultimately lay the foundation for the vast Habsburg Empire. **

Innsbruck: The Stage for a Royal Romance

** In **1477**, just months after her father’s death in the **Battle of Nancy**, the 19-year-old **Maria von Burgund** arrived in **Innsbruck** to meet her betrothed, **Maximilian**. Their union was not just a political alliance but also a love story that unfolded against the stunning backdrop of the **Tiroler Alps**. The city, then a modest but strategically important stronghold, became the setting for one of history’s most consequential royal weddings. **

Where History Comes Alive

** Today, visitors can retrace the footsteps of **Maria von Burgund** in **Innsbruck**: - **Hofburg Innsbruck** – The imperial palace where **Maximilian I** and **Maria von Burgund** were married in a lavish ceremony. The **Silberne Hochzeit** (Silver Wedding) of the couple in **1493** further cemented their legacy. - **Goldenes Dachl** – A breathtaking golden-roofed building commissioned by **Maximilian I** as a symbol of Habsburg power. Its intricate craftsmanship reflects the opulence of the era. - **St. Nikolaus Kirche** – The church where **Maria von Burgund** was laid to rest after her tragic death in a riding accident in **1482**. Her tomb remains a poignant reminder of her brief but impactful life. - **Ambras Castle** – A Renaissance gem where **Maximilian I** later resided, showcasing the couple’s artistic and cultural patronage. **

A Culinary Journey Through Time

** No visit to **Tirol** is complete without savoring its rich culinary traditions. While **Maria von Burgund** may not have enjoyed **Tiroler Gröstl** or **Kaiserschmarrn** (both later staples of **Tiroler** cuisine), her court would have relished in hearty **Burgundian** dishes and fine wines. Today, **Innsbruck**’s restaurants serve up a mix of **Tiroler** classics and international flavors—perfect for modern travelers eager to taste history. **

Plan Your Visit

** Whether you’re a history buff, a culture enthusiast, or simply a traveler seeking inspiration, **Innsbruck** offers a perfect blend of medieval grandeur and alpine beauty. Explore the legacy of **Maria von Burgund**, wander through **Tirol**’s fairy-tale landscapes, and indulge in the region’s legendary hospitality. **

Come and experience why Innsbruck is more than just a city—it’s a living chapter of European history.
